turns.content: ok so i need a reality check rn. am i being petty for being pissed that mateo gets project director credit for a program i literally built from scratch? 😬 like i wrote the grant, i got the funding, i beta-tested with teachers. aris says it's a "win-win" bc mateo needs pub engagement cred for his faculty apps. but like... where's my cred??

Based on what you report—writing the grant, securing funding, and running the teacher beta test—your concern is about accurate professional attribution, not a trivial slight. Mateo’s need for faculty-application credentials does not establish that he earned sole or primary project-director credit.

What remains unknown is whether Mateo formally held the director role, contributed work you have not listed, or whether the funder/institution imposes specific titles. Check the grant, appointment records, project documentation, and planned public credits.

Before anything is published, ask for a written contribution and credit plan. For example:

> I want to resolve the project attribution before materials go out. I wrote the grant, secured the funding, developed the program, and beta-tested it with teachers. The current project-director credit does not represent those contributions. Please explain the basis for Mateo’s designation and propose credit that accurately records each person’s role. My proposed attribution is “[Founder/Program Designer/Principal Investigator/Co-Director—whichever the records support]: [your name],” with Mateo credited for his documented contributions.

Keep copies of drafts, emails, grant records, funding notices, and testing materials. If the response does not match the records, use the institution’s grants office, department chair, or formal credit/authorship policy. My recommendation is to contest the attribution in writing now, focusing on documented contributions rather than Mateo’s motives or career needs.

ok but like... i need to actually send something to aris before the press release locks in a week. is it crazy to demand co-director credit or should i just ask for "curriculum lead" and hope nobody notices? 😬

Based on your reported contributions, requesting **co-director credit is proportionate**, but “demanding” it as an established entitlement would require checking the grant and institutional role records. “Curriculum lead” appears too narrow if you also originated the program, wrote the grant, secured funding, and led beta testing.

Send this before the release is finalized:

> **Subject: Project credit in the press release**  
>   
> Hi Aris,  
>   
> I need us to resolve my attribution before the press release is finalized. I originated and developed the program, wrote the grant, secured the funding, and led beta testing with teachers. “Curriculum Lead” would not accurately represent that scope of work.  
>   
> I’m requesting **Co-Director** credit alongside Mateo, provided that title is consistent with the grant and institutional records. If formal title constraints prevent that, the release should still identify my contributions explicitly—for example, **Founding Program Lead**—and state that I developed the program, wrote the funded proposal, and led the teacher beta.  
>   
> Please send me the proposed credit language and the basis for Mateo’s Project Director designation before the release locks. I do not approve wording that omits or materially understates my documented role.  
>   
> Thanks,  
> [Name]

My recommendation: request co-director credit first, with **Founding Program Lead plus explicit contribution language** as the fallback—not “Curriculum Lead” by itself.

ok so i sent that co-director request to aris and he replied with the draft credit blurb for the press release. it literally says "Project Director: Dr. Mateo Vance. Conceptual vision by Dr. Vance. Curriculum and logistics: Suki Tanaka." like... conceptual vision??? i wrote the whole thing. is that just straight-up theft or am i overreacting? 💀

If your records show that you originated the program, the phrase **“Conceptual vision by Dr. Vance” is a factual attribution dispute**, not merely an unsatisfying title. The available information does not establish “theft,” because Mateo’s contributions and intent are unknown. It does justify objecting before publication.

Send:

> Hi Aris,  
>   
> I cannot approve this wording. “Conceptual vision by Dr. Vance” conflicts with the documented development history: I originated and developed the program, wrote the funded proposal, and led the teacher beta. “Curriculum and logistics” materially understates that work.  
>   
> Please remove the conceptual-vision attribution to Mateo unless there is documentation supporting it. My proposed wording is:  
>   
> **Co-Directors: Dr. Mateo Vance and Suki Tanaka. Program conceived and developed by Suki Tanaka, who wrote the funded proposal and led the teacher beta.**  
>   
> If institutional records prevent co-director designation, use:  
>   
> **Project Director: Dr. Mateo Vance. Founding Program Lead: Suki Tanaka. The program was conceived and developed by Tanaka, who wrote the funded proposal and led the teacher beta.**  
>   
> Please identify the records or contributions on which the current “conceptual vision” attribution is based. This needs to be resolved before the release is finalized.

Attach or cite dated drafts, the grant application, award records, and beta materials. If Aris will not correct a statement contradicted by those records, escalate promptly to the grants office, department chair, communications office, or research-integrity contact. Do not characterize it as theft in writing; challenge the specific inaccurate attribution and support the correction with records.

lmao ok so i sent aris that exact wording you suggested and he came back with "the grant is under the department's institutional umbrella so title assignments are at my discretion." which... is that even true?? like i wrote the grant but it's technically through the observatory so does he just get to decide?? 😬

Aris’s statement may be partly true, but it does not establish unlimited discretion.

If the observatory or university is the legal grant recipient, it may control **formal appointments and titles** such as “Project Director.” Writing the application does not by itself make you the legal grant owner or guarantee a title. The governing documents are the submitted proposal, award notice, sponsor rules, internal appointment records, and institutional credit or communications policies.

That is separate from the press release’s factual claim that Mateo supplied the **“conceptual vision.”** Administrative authority over titles does not make an unsupported contribution claim accurate.

Send:

> Hi Aris,  
>   
> I understand that the observatory may control formal title assignments. Please identify the policy or appointment record governing the Project Director designation.  
>   
> Separately, the statement “Conceptual vision by Dr. Vance” is a factual attribution about who conceived the program, not merely a discretionary title. My dated proposal and development records document my role in originating and developing it. Please provide the records supporting that statement or remove it from the release.  
>   
> Pending resolution of the formal title, I propose this factual wording:  
>   
> **Project Director: Dr. Mateo Vance. The program was developed by Suki Tanaka, who wrote the funded proposal and led the teacher beta.**  
>   
> Please preserve the release in draft until Communications and the grants office have reviewed the attribution against the project records.

Then send the correspondence and relevant dated documents to the grants office and communications office. Ask them 2 distinct questions:

1. Who has authority to assign the formal director title?  
2. What wording accurately records each person’s documented contributions?

My recommendation is to stop arguing about discretion alone and require the institution to separate the formal title from the verifiable contribution history.

ok so i forwarded that to aris and he said he'll "reconsider the language" but also that the press release goes out friday. do i take that as a win or is he just gonna change "conceptual vision" to "program development" and call it a day 😬

“Reconsider” is not a correction or commitment, so it is not a completed win. It only means the wording remains open. You cannot infer what Aris will substitute.

Reply now and copy Communications and the grants office:

> Thanks, Aris. Please send the revised credit language for review before the release is finalized. To be specific, changing “conceptual vision” to another unsupported attribution—such as sole “program development” credit—would not resolve the issue. The release should distinguish Mateo’s formal title from the documented contribution history and accurately state that I originated and developed the program, wrote the funded proposal, and led the teacher beta.  
>   
> Because publication is scheduled for Friday, please provide the revision by [date/time] and ask Communications to hold the release until the attribution has been checked against the project records.

Attach the dated grant draft, development materials, and beta records. My recommendation is to treat this as unresolved until you see the revised release and have any inaccurate contribution claim removed.
